bet.text: A tall robot with a big drum shooter and a hopper of around 80 fuel, which the team felt was really versatile.

demand.text: The team thought a turret would not suit its play style, did not think going under the trench a good play style at the time, and felt defense would not be extreme; it says it was somewhat correct.

auto.text: Autos were made only in the PathPlanner GUI and cross the bump several times, with three Limelights correcting the pose.
After a crossing it drives to a point before shooting, with a timeout. Time-based paths give up and return, which makes them easier to coordinate with partners.

cycle.text: Fuel goes past a kicker bar and main roller into the extending hopper, across a rolling floor, and up a roller elevator to the drum.
In one match a host describes it filling the hopper, sending a salvo, while 2056 picks up the pockets left over.

endgame.text: No climber: one added on March 1 was removed by March 19, before the first event, for weight, and stayed off because of how the game developed.

gave_up.text: It could only cross the bump. Posters say tall robots were easy to exploit and that it struggled under more defense at the championship.
In Ontario, hosts say, 2056 pushed defenders aside so it could cross, and it was perhaps heavy enough to push through.
It gave up the climber; the weight went to rollers.

changed.text: After the first event an active wall went in front of the shooter tower, then passive side rollers, against bridging fuel.
Rollers were switched to grip tape, which raised accuracy and rate of fire.
The kicker bar, first a cloth with a metal bar that stayed out, now folds in with the hopper when crossing the bump.

outcome.text: 62-7-0 in official play; finalist in the Archimedes division; ranked 23 by championship OPR (281.95, Archimedes).

functions.name: Intake and kicker bar

solves.text: Feed the hopper, and fold in to cross the bump

functions.type: front roller intake on an extending hopper

facts.text: Two Kraken X60s
Silicone roller, with safety walk on the kicker bar
The intake can vibrate, to push balls faster into the indexer or to free a robot stuck on the bump or beached
The team thanks 1678 for help with its intake iterations

functions.name: Extending hopper

solves.text: Hold a lot of fuel and feed it at a steady rate without bridging

functions.type: tall extending hopper with active floor and roller walls

facts.text: Holds around
The top cover was inspired by the "magic blanket" claw of 1124 in 2008
Active floor rollers keep balls from settling on each other
An active wall in front of the shooter tower and passive rollers on the sides stop fuel bridging there
The top two rollers on the left and right spin freely; a bottom roller is powered by a Kraken X44 through a belt across the robot
Roller wall and side rollers are covered in cat tongue
Fewer places where balls touch a surface that does not roll made the fire rate more consistent, without raising its high end much

cost.text: Bridged fuel was a huge limit on fire rate: output could drop until all the balls in the hopper suddenly fell and the rate returned

functions.name: Roller elevator and drum shooter

solves.text: Feed fuel to the drum faster

functions.type: roller elevator feeding a big drum with a hood

facts.text: 3 in compliant wheels feed an elevator of belted rollers up to the drum
Rollers with cat tongue push balls down towards the shooter, added because of trouble feeding faster
After the switch to skateboard grip tape, shooting accuracy rose from about 80% to around 95 to 98%
The same switch added about 2 to 3 balls per second
The grip tape never had to be cleaned; only the shooter tape was changed, before the world championship

cost.text: The biggest risk of grip tape is damaging fuel, so any place where fuel could stall stayed cat tongue or silicone

solves.text: Know the pose after impacts and after crossing the bump

facts.text: Three Limelights; MegaTag2 is always active, MegaTag1 only zeros the gyro before the robot is first enabled
The shooter camera is trusted greatly when it sees three or more tags, to make aiming more consistent
Trust in the cameras was tuned between a noisy pose and a delay before an accurate pose after the bump
A lookup gives RPM and angle for passing and scoring
LEDs show aim, zeroing and other states
Code is a slightly modified AdvantageKit CTRE swerve template with a team wrapper for PID control and logging
A poster quotes a method in the released code that drives with the center of rotation around the intake

decisions.because: holding around 80 fuel was a good trade-off
decisions.instead_of: a turret, or a robot that goes under the trench

decisions.because: it was too heavy before the first event, and the game developed so that it stayed off
accuracy and balls per second rose after switching and it never needed cleaning
decisions.cost: a risk of damaging fuel where it stalls

decisions.because: fuel covers a large area with several tags always in view, and it was the quickest way in a first command-based season

decisions.choice: Kicker bar joined to the hopper
decisions.because: it folds in with the hopper when crossing the bump
decisions.instead_of: a cloth with a metal bar that dropped at the start and stayed out
